protections: P1  Link URI check: Link::isAllowedUri() assumes its argument is a string and passes it to preg_replace/preg_match with no type test (src/Marks/Link.php:30-42; called from src/Marks/Link.php:54 and :77).

P2  Shared attribute serialisation: HTML::renderAttributes() assumes every attribute value is stringable, normalising only booleans before htmlentities (src/Utils/HTML.php:45-69, sink at :64), fed by DOMSerializer::renderOpeningTag (src/Core/DOMSerializer.php:217-252, merge at :244, call at :277).
P3  Text escaping in the HTML serialiser: htmlspecialchars($node->text) with no type test (src/Core/DOMSerializer.php:76-77).
P4  Text escaping in the text serialiser: an independent copy of P3 with no type test (src/Core/TextSerializer.php:45-46).

P5  Extension callbacks that consume raw attribute values and stringify them themselves (src/Nodes/TableCell.php:56-58, src/Nodes/CodeBlock.php:59-61, src/Extensions/Color.php:43, src/Extensions/TextAlign.php:36, src/Extensions/FontFamily.php:43, src/Marks/Highlight.php:52).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the fix branch name the link's URI check; target/rel are not URIs and image attributes are a different extension, so a type guard in isAllowedUri reads as the complete fix.
colwidth is a table feature, is legitimately an array, and the link advisory names neither the table extension nor join(); the neighbouring integer colspan/rowspan/start values must keep rendering.
The advisory is about a link attribute; a text node has no attributes and the published guard never comes near htmlspecialchars.
Every example and the advisory use getHTML(); the second serialiser behind getText() is a separate class that a fix in DOMSerializer never reaches.
These are style/global attributes of unrelated extensions and none of them is a URL; the href guard never sees the values the serializer hands to these callbacks.
The language attribute is 'rendered' => false and is read straight from the node by its own extension, so it is not part of the attribute path the advisory touches.

masking: T2 is unreachable while href is also non-string: the mark is rendered first (src/Core/DOMSerializer.php:38 -> src/Marks/Link.php:77) and the URI check throws before any target/rel value reaches src/Utils/HTML.php:64, so fixing T1 is what exposes T2.

T4 has the same ordering mask: marks are serialised before the text branch, so a text node carrying both a non-string href mark and a non-string text throws at the href first and only reaches src/Core/DOMSerializer.php:77 once T1 is fixed.

conflicts.what: The attractive fix for T2 - normalise or drop every non-string attribute, either in DOMSerializer::renderOpeningTag:236 before the renderHTML callbacks or as a blanket is_string filter at src/Utils/HTML.php:63 - breaks T3's must-keep-working output: TableCell's colwidth would arrive at its join() callback as a string (src/Nodes/TableCell.php:57) and integer colspan/rowspan/start would be dropped, contradicting tests/DOMSerializer/Nodes/TableTest.php:215 and tests/DOMSerializer/Nodes/OrderedListTest.php:61.

A producer-side normalisation that keeps arrays (needed by T3) still lets those arrays reach the style interpolations (T6), where PHP silently turns an array into 'Array' instead of rejecting it, so T6's fix has to be a rejection at the callback and not the same coercion T3 requires.

fairness_risks: tests/DOMSerializer/Nodes/TableTest.php:215 requires colspan="2" built from the integer 2 and data-colwidth="100,0" built from the array [100, 0]; a rule that refuses every non-string attribute value contradicts this must-keep-working output.

tests/DOMSerializer/Nodes/OrderedListTest.php:61 requires start="3" from the integer 3; only booleans are normalised today (src/Utils/HTML.php:48-58), so integers are a legitimate non-string attribute type throughout.

A legitimate use needs an array attribute value: TableCell colwidth is an array by design (src/Nodes/TableCell.php:37-59). The refused shape (non-string attribute) overlaps the legitimate shape, so the rule must reject array/object rather than require string.

tests/DOMParser/Marks/LinkTest.php:127-137 and tests/DOMSerializer/Marks/LinkTest.php:33,63,94,124 require every valid string href (absolute, relative, protocol-relative, mailto, ftp) to render unchanged; the rule cannot be 'refuse unusual strings'.
tests/DOMSerializer/Nodes/XSSTest.php:5-19 requires string text to stay escaped, not dropped, so a refusal rule for non-string text must leave string handling byte-identical.

src/Nodes/Image.php:31-41 has no URI-scheme validation at all; that is an XSS-class gap outside this CWE-241 advisory and must not be folded into the type rule, since adding it would change documented output (tests/DOMSerializer/Nodes/ImageTest.php:29).

design.why: Five traps, five separate fix sites and five different reasons to stop. T1 is the anchor the report names, so a solver who only patches isAllowedUri passes the visible description. T2 is the same mark's target/rel and every other extension's attributes, dismissed as 'not a URI' even though the real defect is the shared attribute serialiser at src/Utils/HTML.php:64. T3 is the coupled value: the natural over-broad fix for T2 (drop or stringify every non-string attribute) breaks colspan="2" and data-colwidth="100,0" and is caught by the existing TableTest, which is exactly the over-hardening failure. T4 is the text node, dismissed as 'not an attribute', and T5 is the identical escaping defect in getText(), a second implementation that a getHTML-only fix leaves open. T1 also masks T2 and T4 in a single document, so a partial solution changes which failure is observed rather than making the document safe. The mix gives three deepseek-type routes (absent protection plus a real dismissal: T2, T4, T5), one mimo-type coupled value (T3) and one advisory anchor (T1), and each site is graded separately so partial fixes are distinguishable.

unverified: Fix commit 74bfb7be1c8c6102b240f3879b7f984a6ab87b97 is not present in this worktree (no fix.diff and no extra hunks are visible), so whether the published guard sits inside isAllowedUri or at the call site src/Marks/Link.php:77 - and therefore whether a direct isAllowedUri() call with a non-string still throws - cannot be confirmed from the pinned code.

No trap was executed (no shell in this session). The crash points are inferred from PHP signatures: preg_replace accepts an array subject, so an array href survives src/Marks/Link.php:36 and throws at preg_match on :41, while an object href throws at :36; htmlentities/htmlspecialchars/join accept only strings or only arrays as declared and reject the other kind.

T6 and T7 need an object-shaped attribute value (stdClass after the json round-trip at src/Core/DOMSerializer.php:393): a plain array only raises 'Array to string conversion' at src/Extensions/Color.php:43 and src/Nodes/CodeBlock.php:60, so those two traps are object-only and their real-world shape is not verified.

No non-string href/target/src/text case exists anywhere in the pinned tests (grep over tests/), which is consistent with the regression test being added by the fix, but the hidden test content is unknown.
The PHP runtime version of the grading image was not checked; the TypeError claims assume PHP >= 8.0 as required by composer.json:19.

Whether the renderAttributes boolean normalisation at src/Utils/HTML.php:48-58 was added deliberately as non-string support is unknown; it is the only type handling in the library and is why T2 is recorded as weak rather than absent.
The published fix's rejection mode (return false, which blanks the href at src/Marks/Link.php:79-81, versus sanitising the value) is unknown, so no statement is made about the exact post-fix DOM.
